newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Ciba seeks five pct assets cut in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Ciba seeks five pct assets cut in 1997.

text.p: Ciba Specialty Chemicals Holding Inc Chairman Rolf Meyer said the company being spun off from Novartis AG planned to cut its total assets by around five percent this year by getting a better grip on inventories.
He also told financial analysts that the company aimed to have each of its five divisions post returns above the cost of capital, which it now calculates at nine percent.

"We are not yet happy with the assets management, particularly the inventory management in the company, and also to some extent the fixed-asset levels and the capital expenditure programmes," he said.

"We are addressing this with two additional objectives in 1997. We want to reduce assets overall by five percent and in the medium term we want to limit capital expenditure to an order of six percent of sales."
Meyer said Ciba sought to improve its financial performance.

"We are starting from a strong base but we are not yet happy with our financial performance and we want to set more ambitious objectives," he said in a presentation by senior managers before the spin-off, which is Europe's largest.

"We want to go for sales growth that is above market growth and we are confident that should achieve that with the innovative products that we have," he said. Sales topped 6.7 billion Swiss francs in 1996.

He reiterated the company's goal of hitting earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) of 15 percent of sales in 1997, growing to 18 to 20 percent in the next three to four years if not earlier.
The depreciation component would be around five to six percent, he said.

The total 1995 operating margin was eight percent of sales. EBIT by sector ranged from 21 percent for additives to minus three percent for textile dyes. Pigments returned 18 percent, polymers 11 percent and consumer care chemicals three percent.

"Textile dyes and consumer care chemicals are still some way away from where we would like to see competitive performance. In all, every division over time should have a return above the cost of capital. That is a minimum requirement," he said.

Meyer said Ciba was reviewing growth options in individual business. It aims to expand its strong position in Europe and North America. "We also see attractive expansion possibilities in Asia, the emerging markets and also Latin America," he said.
Organic growth will depend on innovative products, he said, adding Ciba would invest four to five percent of sales in research and development.

"We want to supplement internal growth with selective external growth," he added. "We see licensing as a possibility here, but we also see acquistitions and potentially alliances. We will follow that in a disciplined way."
Such transactions would have to generate value over and above the nine percent cost of capital, he said.

"We would also shoot for transactions where there is a strategic fit or where there is a possibility to create sustainable competitive advantage based on key core competences that we already have or that we can develop," he said.
